IRON BISGLYCINATE
Ferrous bisglycinate chelate is iron bound to two molecules of glycine, an amino acid.
Ferrochel® is a branded version of this form, and we name it on the front of the pack.
The label states the elemental iron per capsule, 29 mg, so you know exactly how much iron you get rather than the weight of the compound.
The label also explains when to take it and what to avoid alongside.

Read: Why Body Café Co. exists
Form. Amount. Moment. Proof.
1

It starts with the form.
The same nutrient can come in very different forms, so we name the one we chose, every time. If a form was chosen for a reason, you deserve to see it.

2

Then the amount.
Every label states how much is in a serving, ingredient by ingredient. There are no hidden blends and no totals that could mean anything.

3

Then the moment.
A supplement only earns its place if it fits into a real day, so every bottle tells you when to take it, whether to take it with food, and what to keep apart.

4

And then the proof.
Our products are made in GMP-certified facilities in Gujarat, by manufacturers we name on every pack. They are third-party tested. Their ingredients are traceable. Scan the code on any bottle and there is more to read.

Read: The thinking behind our products

bodyText:
OUR STORY

You should always know what you're being served.

A good café shows you the menu. So do we.

I

Careful people.

Think about how carefully you choose things.

You check the expiry date on the milk packet. You read three reviews before buying a phone cover. You ask the chemist which brand to take, and then you ask a friend whether the chemist is right. When something goes into your body, or into your family's, you want to know what it is.

And then there is the supplement shelf.

II

An opaque shelf.

It is loud. Every bottle promises more energy, more strength, more glow. The front of the label shouts and the back of it whispers. The facts that matter most are buried in small type, folded into a "proprietary blend", or missing altogether: what form the ingredient is in, how much of it you actually get, and when you should take it.

Advice arrives from everywhere: a forwarded message, a trainer at the gym, a relative who swears by something. Most of it is well meant. Very little of it is clear.

So people do one of two things. They buy on faith and hope it works. Or they quietly give up, because it was never clear why they started.

Neither is a real choice. A choice needs information.

III

Why Body Café Co. exists.

Body Café Co. began with a simple belief: you should always know exactly what you are taking, and why.

It is the idea behind every good café. You can read the menu. You can see what goes into your cup. Nobody hides the recipe, because the recipe is the reason you walked in. We wanted supplements to feel like that: open, specific, and made with care for the person who will actually use them.

That belief shapes everything we make.

Today's menu
AMOUNT PER SERVING

800 mg omega-3
EPA 400 · DHA 300 · as triglycerides

29 mg iron

2000 mg husk

Every amount above is stated in full. No hidden blends.

IV

The thinking behind our products.
1

It starts with the form.
The same nutrient can come in very different forms, so we name the one we chose, every time. If a form was chosen for a reason, you deserve to see it.

2

Then the amount.
Every label states how much is in a serving, ingredient by ingredient. There are no hidden blends and no totals that could mean anything.

3

Then the moment.
A supplement only earns its place if it fits into a real day, so every bottle tells you when to take it, whether to take it with food, and what to keep apart.

4

And then the proof.
Our products are made in GMP-certified facilities in Gujarat, by manufacturers we name on every pack. They are third-party tested. Their ingredients are traceable. Scan the code on any bottle and there is more to read.

PRODUCT	THE DECISION	WHY WE SHOW IT

Vitamin D3 + K2
	D3 and K2 (as MK-7) in a softgel of omega-3 oil, not a dry tablet	Both vitamins are fat-soluble; the label asks you to take it with food

Omega-3 Fish Oil
	Omega-3 as triglycerides; oil and omega-3 listed separately	So 1000 mg of oil is never mistaken for 1000 mg of omega-3

Iron Bisglycinate
	Ferrochel® ferrous bisglycinate chelate; elemental iron stated	You see the iron you get (29 mg), plus when to take it and what to avoid

Psyllium Husk (Isabgol)
	Familiar isabgol, measured into capsules	Every serving is the same: 2000 mg, with water, at night

Myo & D-Chiro Inositol
	Both forms listed separately, 40:1 ratio on the front	A single total would hide how much of each you get

Creatine Chews
	Creatine monohydrate as an orange chew; added sugar printed	Easier to take every day, and you should know about the sugar too

V

What we believe.

We believe the form of an ingredient deserves a name.

We believe an amount should be a number, not a blend.

We believe “when” and “with what” matter as much as “what”.

We believe a label is a promise you should be able to check.

We believe in a short shelf, made with care.

VI

What we can demonstrate.
AMOUNTS

Every active ingredient listed with its own amount per serving, on every label.

FORMS

The form of each ingredient named on the pack.

DIRECTIONS

When and how to take each product, printed on the bottle.

MAKERS

Asoj Soft Caps (Baroda), Vebe Lifecare (Baroda), U-Liva Nutrition (Rajkot), all GMP-certified.

STANDARDS

%RDA values calculated as per ICMR 2020 guidelines where established.

LICENCE

FSSAI licence for Bluebell Lifecare Pvt. Ltd.: 10726994000121.

VII

Our place in everyday life.

None of this is complicated. That is the point. Care, done properly, usually looks simple from the outside.

We do not think supplements should take over your life. They are a small part of it: a softgel with breakfast, a few capsules before bed, a habit that sits quietly between the alarm and the first meeting of the day. A good life is built mostly elsewhere, in meals and sleep, in movement, in time with the people you love. Our job is to make the small part honest, so you can stop thinking about it and get on with the rest.

So we keep our shelf short and make each product with care. We would rather explain one thing well than sell you ten things you do not understand. If a question is not answered on the label, ask us, and expect an answer you can check.

Because trust is not built by promises. It is built by being able to look.

We don't make loud promises.

We don't hide behind small print.

We don't sell miracles in a bottle.

We name the form. We state the amount. We tell you when. We show our work.

Read the label. Ask your question. Take what makes sense for you.

BUILT ON RESEARCH. MADE FOR REAL LIFE.

ABOUT BODY CAFÉ CO.

Who we are, and how we work.

WHY WE EXIST

The front of the label shouts. The back whispers.

More energy.
More strength.
More glow.

You check the date on the milk packet. You read reviews before buying a phone cover. Then you reach the supplement shelf, and the facts that matter most are in tiny type, inside a "blend", or missing.

Advice arrives from every direction, and very little of it is clear. So people either buy on faith, or quietly stop. Neither is a real choice. A choice needs information.

WHY WE EXIST

Most supplement shopping asks for trust first and offers detail later, if at all. We think it should work the other way round.

Before you choose, you should be able to see what's in a product, in what form, and where the record for your bottle lives. You don't need a science degree. You do deserve straight answers, in plain English first.

We'd like supplements to feel less clinical and more like something you can talk about. But a light tone is never a reason to blur a fact. If something isn't confirmed yet, we say so plainly.

WHY COLOUR?

We start with seven everyday supplements. Each is named for what's in it, and each has its own cap colour, so the range is easy to read from across the room.

WHY “CAFÉ”

A good café is an everyday place. Nobody minds if you ask what's in something, and the menu tells you before you order.

That's the counter we want to run: unhurried, curious and specific. The café isn't a theme. It's a standard for how a shop should treat a question.

There's no café to visit. The name describes how we want to treat your questions, wherever you shop with us.

HOW WE BEHAVE

title: The words on the label — Body Café Co.
bodyText:
Learn
Glossary

GLOSSARY

The words on the label

Plain definitions for the terms used across our guides. Each links to the guide that explains it in full.

Filter terms

29 terms

A
Allergen statement
Tells you whether a product contains a common allergen, such as fish. Read it before you buy. Read more
Amino acid
A building-block molecule. L-theanine and glycine are amino acids; L-theanine isn't used to build proteins. Read more
Amount per serving
How much of an ingredient one serving contains, with its unit. Read more
C
Certification
A third party's statement that a product or site met a defined standard, for a defined scope and period. Read more
Chelate / bisglycinate
A mineral bound to another molecule. “Bisglycinate” means bound to two molecules of the amino acid glycine. Read more
Creatine monohydrate
The most widely used and studied form of creatine; 88% creatine by weight. Read more
D
Detection level
The lowest amount a method can detect. “Not detected” only means something next to it. Read more
E
Elemental amount
For minerals, the amount of the mineral itself, as opposed to the weight of the whole compound it's bound in. Read more
EPA and DHA
Eicosapentaenoic acid and docosahexaenoic acid: the long-chain omega-3s a fish oil label should state separately. Read more
H
Health supplement
In India, a category of food regulated by FSSAI. Labels must carry the words “HEALTH SUPPLEMENT” and “NOT FOR MEDICINAL USE”. Read more
I
Ingredient form
The specific compound used, such as a particular salt, chelate or ester. It's part of the ingredient's identity. Read more
IU (International Unit)
A unit used for some vitamins. For vitamin D, 1 mcg equals 40 IU. Read more
L
“L-” in a name
Marks one of two mirror-image forms of a molecule. It's part of the ingredient's name, not a brand prefix. Read more
Lot number
The code that links a pack to its manufacturing batch. Not the same as an order number or barcode. Read more
O
Observational study
A study that watches what people already do. It can show links, not prove cause. Read more
Other ingredients
Everything in the product besides the headline ingredients: shells, fillers, sweeteners, flavours. Read more
P
Psyllium husk
The seed coats of the Plantago ovata plant, also called ispaghula husk. Read more
R
Randomised controlled trial
A study that assigns people by chance to receive something or a comparison, to test cause and effect. Read more
S
Sample
The portion of a lot that was actually tested. Read more
Serving size
The amount the label's numbers refer to, such as one capsule or two chews. Always read amounts together with it. Read more
Servings per pack
How many servings the pack holds. Units in the pack ÷ units per serving. Read more
Specification
The reviewed limits a result is compared against. Without one, a result can't be called a pass. Read more
Stereoisomer
Molecules with the same atoms arranged differently in space. Myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol are two stereoisomers of inositol. Read more
Systematic review
A study that gathers and appraises all the research on a question using a set method. Read more
T
Test method
The named procedure a laboratory used. A result means little without it. Read more
Triglyceride form
One chemical form omega-3s come in. Others include ethyl esters, re-esterified triglycerides, free fatty acids and phospholipids. Read more
U
Units (g, mg, mcg)
1 g = 1,000 mg and 1 mg = 1,000 mcg. Compare amounts only in the same unit. Read more
V
Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol)
One of the two main forms of vitamin D in supplements; the other is D2 (ergocalciferol). Read more
Vitamin K2 (menaquinones)
A family of vitamin K forms named MK-4 to MK-13. Vitamin K1 is phylloquinone. Read more

In short
We deliver across India through our courier partners.
Delivery is ₹75 per order, and free when your subtotal after discount is ₹1,499 or more.
Every order is prepaid. Cash on delivery isn’t available.
If a parcel is late, lost, damaged or incomplete, tell us within 7 days of delivery and we’ll put it right.

Your orders
Report a delivery problem

Where we deliver #

We deliver to pincodes across India that our courier partners serve. Enter your pincode in your bag or at checkout; if we can’t deliver there, we tell you before you pay.

When orders are sent #

We pack orders Monday to Saturday, except public holidays, and hand them to our courier partner. Your order page shows when it has shipped.

Delivery charges #

Delivery is ₹75 per order. It’s free when your subtotal, after any discount, is ₹1,499 or more.

The delivery charge is shown in your bag and at checkout, included in a single total, before you pay.

Delivery estimates #

Delivery time depends on your pincode and the courier. Any date we show is an estimate, not a promise. Remote areas can take longer.

Tracking #

When your order ships, its page shows the courier, the tracking number and the courier’s updates.

Changing the delivery address #

Before dispatch, contact us with your order reference and the new address. The change is made once we confirm it on your case. After dispatch, it depends on the courier; we’ll ask them for you.

Failed delivery and return to us #

If the courier can’t deliver after its attempts and the parcel comes back to us, we contact you and agree whether to send it again or refund the order.

Late, lost, damaged or incomplete parcels #

Tell us within 7 days of delivery from the order page or the contact form, with your order reference. A photo helps with damage but isn’t required.

If goods arrive damaged, wrong, defective or late, you’re entitled to a refund or replacement. Nothing in this policy limits your rights under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and its rules.

Cash on delivery #

Cash on delivery isn’t available. Pay online by UPI, card, wallet or net banking.

Help with a delivery #

Use Contact and choose “An order: delivery, tracking or address”. We reply Monday to Saturday, 10:00–18:00 IST, within one business day.

Still need help?

Contact us and we’ll pick it up from here. You get a case reference straight away.

Contact support

Print this page
In short
If something arrives damaged, wrong, missing, faulty or expired, tell us within 7 days of delivery and we’ll arrange a refund or replacement.
We don’t accept change-of-mind returns: supplements are consumed, so we only take back items with a problem.
Approved refunds go back to the original payment method within 7 business days.
Product safety concerns are handled separately, as a priority.

Your orders
Report a safety concern

Damaged, wrong, missing, faulty or expired items #

Start a request from the order page. Choose the item, what went wrong and whether you’d prefer a refund or a replacement.

We don’t refuse a refund or replacement for goods that are defective, deficient, spurious, not as described or delivered late.

Change of mind #

We don’t accept returns of items you no longer want. Supplements are consumed, and we can’t resell a returned pack safely. This doesn’t affect items that arrive with a problem.

Time limit #

Tell us within 7 days of delivery. If you notice a problem later, such as a fault inside a sealed pack, contact us anyway and we’ll look at it.

Condition of items #

Keep the pack, its seal and the lot number if you can. It helps us trace the batch.

How to ask #

From your order page choose “Report a problem with this order”, or use Contact with your order reference. You get a case reference straight away and can follow progress in your account.

Photos and evidence #

A photo of the damage, the item and the lot number helps us act faster. It isn’t required, and we won’t refuse a request just because you don’t have one.

Sending items back #

If we need the item back, we arrange a pickup through our courier partner at no cost to you. Please don’t send anything until we’ve confirmed the pickup on your case.

Refunds #

Refunds go back to the original payment method. We review each request and release approved refunds within 7 business days; the order page shows the status.

After release, UPI refunds usually arrive within a few days. Card and net-banking refunds can take up to 7 business days more, depending on your bank.

Delivery charges, discounts and part-refunds #

When we refund part of an order, we refund what you paid for those items after any discount. If the whole order is refunded because of our mistake or a delivery problem, the delivery charge is refunded too.

Product safety #

If you think a product is unsafe or has made someone unwell, stop using it and report it as a product safety concern. It’s handled as a priority, separately from returns.

Your rights #

Nothing in this policy limits your rights under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020.

Still need help?

Contact us and we’ll pick it up from here. You get a case reference straight away.

Contact support

We use your details to take and deliver orders, run your account, answer support cases and publish reviews you submit.
Marketing and optional analytics are off unless you turn them on, and you can turn them off at any time.
We don’t use advertising or cross-site tracking technologies, and we don’t sell your data.
Signed-in customers can download their data and make privacy requests from their account.

Preferences
Privacy requests

Who we are #

Body Café Co. is a brand of Bluebell Lifecare Pvt. Ltd., Office No. 202, 2nd Floor, Primate, Opp. Mother Milk Palace, Nr. Judges Bungalows Cross Road, Bodakdev, Ahmedabad, Gujarat 380054, India. Our privacy contact is care@bodycafeco.com.

What we collect #
Your mobile number, when you sign in or check out.
Your name, delivery address, optional email and optional GSTIN, when you check out or save an address.
Your orders, payment status and order history. Card and bank details are handled by our payment partner, Razorpay, and never stored by us.
Support cases: what you write, any photos you attach (location and camera details are removed) and our replies.
Reviews and questions you submit, with any photos.
Your choices: marketing and analytics preferences.
A session cookie and some data saved in your browser (your bag, saved items, preferences and drafts).
If you turn on analytics: the names of pages and actions you use on this site.
Where it comes from #

From you, and from your browser when you use the site. Our payment and courier partners also tell us payment and delivery status.

Why we use it #
Orders: to take payment, pack and deliver your order, and handle cancellations, returns and refunds.
Account: to verify your mobile number and keep your orders, addresses and cases together.
Support: to answer and track your cases, including product safety concerns.
Reviews: to check you received the product and to moderate what you post.
Analytics (only if you turn it on): to understand which pages and features are used.
Marketing (only if you turn it on): to tell you about new products and guides by email or WhatsApp.
Legal duties: to keep records the law requires and respond to lawful requests.
Who we share it with #

Each gets only what it needs for that service. We may also share information when the law requires it, for example with tax authorities or in response to a lawful request. We don’t sell personal data.

Razorpay, to take payments and refunds.
Our courier partners, to deliver your order: your name, delivery address and mobile number.
Our SMS provider, to send sign-in codes and order messages.
Netlify and Supabase, which host this website and its database.
Cookies and similar technologies #
Necessary: a session cookie (bcc_session) that keeps you signed in and protects forms. It can’t be turned off.
Necessary: browser storage for your bag, saved items, drafts and preferences.
Optional: first-party analytics that records page and action names, only when you turn it on in Preferences.
We don’t use advertising, personalisation or third-party tracking technologies.
How long we keep it #

You can ask us to delete your data at any time. Records the law requires us to keep are kept for that period only.

Orders, invoices and payment records: 8 years, as tax and company law require.
Your account, addresses and preferences: until you delete your account.
Support cases: as long as needed to resolve them and handle any follow-up, then deleted or anonymised.
Marketing consent: until you withdraw it, plus a record that you did.
Your choices and rights #

Requests are made from your account, so we know they come from you. Each gets a reference you can follow.

See and download a copy of your data (Profile & security › Download my data).
Correct or update your details.
Ask us to delete your account and data.
Withdraw a consent, such as marketing, at any time in Preferences.
Nominate someone to act for you.
Make a privacy complaint.
How we check it’s you #

Privacy requests need you to be signed in with the one-time code sent to your mobile number. We may ask for more information if a request concerns data we can’t link to your number.

Children #

Anyone can browse, but only adults (18 or older) can buy. We don’t knowingly collect personal data from children.

Security and storage #

Sign-in codes are stored only in scrambled (hashed) form and expire after five minutes. Session cookies can’t be read by page scripts, forms are protected against cross-site requests, and photos are checked and stripped of location data before they’re stored. No system is perfectly secure, and we’ll tell you if a breach affects your data.

Our hosting providers may store or process data outside India. Where they do, they protect it to the same standard as this policy.

The law we follow #

Today, the Information Technology Act, 2000 and the Information Technology (Reasonable Security Practices and Procedures and Sensitive Personal Data or Information) Rules, 2011 apply. Most duties under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 begin on 13 May 2027, and this policy will be updated before then.

Privacy contact and grievances #

Make a privacy request from your account, or use Contact and choose “A privacy request”.

Grievance Officer: Nayan Solanki, Grievance Officer, Bluebell Lifecare Pvt. Ltd., Office No. 202, 2nd Floor, Primate, Opp. Mother Milk Palace, Nr. Judges Bungalows Cross Road, Bodakdev, Ahmedabad, Gujarat 380054. Email care@bodycafeco.com, phone +91-9274248974 (Monday to Saturday, 10:00–18:00 IST). We acknowledge a grievance within 48 hours and resolve it within one month.

Changes to this policy #

When this policy changes in a way that matters, we’ll update the version and date at the top and tell signed-in customers.

Still need help?

Contact us and we’ll pick it up from here. You get a case reference straight away.

What a lot report shows

ESSENTIALS

What a lot report shows

The difference between a product, a manufacturing lot and a tested sample.

2 min read
Body Café Co. editorial
Not yet specialist-reviewed
Version 0.1 · 22 October 2026

Save guide
Print learning sheet
Copy link

IN THIS GUIDE

1
In a minute
2
A product is not a lot
3
What a report should identify
4
Reading a result
5
What a report can't prove
6
What you may see on our lookup
7
Worked example
8
Checklist
9
Sources and versions
In a minute
#

“Tested” can mean almost anything. A good lot report is specific: which batch, which sample, which tests, which limits. This guide explains how to read one, and how to spot what a report can't tell you.

A product is made in many lots; a report describes one.
Results only mean something next to their units and limits.
A pass needs a reviewed specification to compare against.
A report doesn't authenticate an individual pack.

EXAMPLE REPORT ANATOMY · NOT A REAL DOCUMENT · NO RESULTS SHOWN

Product: Example capsules
Lot: EXAMPLE-LOT
Laboratory · date · version
What was tested	Result	Unit	Method	Limit or specification
The ingredient or contaminant measured	The measured value	For example mg per capsule	The named test method used	The range the result is judged against
A report describes a sample from one lot. Read the result together with its unit, method and limit.
A product is not a lot
#

A product is a recipe and a label. A lot (or batch) is one production run of that product. A sample is the portion of a lot that was actually tested. A report should name all three, so you can tell whether it describes the pack in your hand or just the product in general.

What a report should identify
#
The product and lot it describes, matching the lot number on your pack.
The sample: when it was taken and what it was.
Each test performed, and the method used.
Each result, with its unit.
The specification the result is compared against.
The source document, in a version that can be published, with its version and date.

If any of these is missing, the report is telling you less than it seems to.

Reading a result
#

A number on its own isn't a verdict. Read the test, the result, the unit and the limit together. A result described as a “pass” should point to the specification it passed. Where a laboratory reports that something wasn't detected, the report should say what level the method can detect, so you know what “not detected” means for that test.

What a report can't prove
#

A lot report describes a sample from one batch at one time. It isn't a clinical trial, it doesn't predict how a product will work for you, and it doesn't prove that one particular pack is genuine. Research about an ingredient isn't the same thing as testing a finished product, either.

What you may see on our lookup
#

When you look up a lot, the result is one of a few states. Lot found means the lot belongs to the product you chose. No matching lot usually means a typo or the wrong product. Not published yet means a record exists but isn't ready to view; it doesn't mean anything passed or failed. Withdrawn means the lot has been taken off sale and you should follow the instructions shown.

Worked example
#

Fictional example for reading practice only. Not a Body Café Co. result, laboratory or document.

An illustrative result line

Example contaminant screen
Method
Named method reference
Result
Not detected
Detection level
Stated, with unit
Specification
Reviewed limit, with unit
Document
Report version and date

“Not detected” is only meaningful because the detection level is given. The specification tells you what the result is being judged against.

Checklist
#
Product and lot match your pack
Sample described
Each test and method named
Results given with units
Specification stated
Source document and version linked
Limits of the report explained

This guide explains general reading practice and doesn't rely on an external source.

In a minute
#

A supplement label is a short document with a lot to say. Read in the right order, it tells you what you're taking, how much of it, and what to watch for. This guide works for any label, not only ours.

Read every amount together with its serving size.
Look for the full ingredient name, including its form.
Find directions, warnings, allergens and storage before you buy.
Keep the lot number: it links your pack to its batch.

EXAMPLE LABEL · NOT A BODY CAFÉ CO. PRODUCT · AMOUNTS LEFT BLANK ON PURPOSE

EXAMPLE INGREDIENT CAPSULES

2

Ingredient B (as named form)

3

5
LOT ▢▢▢▢▢▢ · EXP ▢▢/▢▢

1
Product name and form
The ingredient named in full, including its form.
2
Serving size
How many units make one serving, and servings per pack.
3
Amount per serving

4

5

6

Printed on the pack. It links the pack to its batch record.
Start with the serving
#

Every amount on a label refers to a serving, and a serving isn't always one unit. If the serving is two capsules, the amount per serving comes from two capsules together. Before comparing two products, check that you're comparing the same thing: the amount per serving, the number of units in that serving, and how many servings are in the pack.

The serving size is set by the label's directions. It isn't a suggestion from us, and it isn't something to work out from the front of the pack.

Read the full ingredient name
#

The headline on the front of a pack is a summary. The ingredient list tells you exactly what's inside, including the form of each ingredient: a mineral as a particular salt or chelate, a vitamin in a named form, an oil with its active fatty acids. The form can change how much of the active ingredient a given weight contains, so it belongs next to the quantity. Our guide to ingredient forms goes further.

Also look at what else is in the product. Capsule shells, softgel materials, sweeteners in chews and other added ingredients should all be listed.

The statements an Indian health supplement label carries
#

In India, health supplements are regulated by FSSAI. Its health-supplement regulations require the label to carry, among other things:

the words “HEALTH SUPPLEMENT”;
the amount of each nutrient or substance with a nutritional or physiological effect;
the advisory “NOT FOR MEDICINAL USE”, displayed prominently;
where applicable, amounts as a percentage of the ICMR recommended daily allowances, with the warning “Not to exceed the recommended daily usage”;
a statement that the product isn't a substitute for a varied diet;
warnings, precautions, known side effects, contraindications and interactions, as applicable;
a statement that the product should be stored out of the reach of children.

The same regulations don't allow a health supplement to claim that it prevents, treats or cures a disease. If a product makes that kind of promise, read it as a warning sign.

This is a reading aid, not a legal assessment. It summarises the regulation text listed in the sources below; check the current consolidated regulations for anything you rely on.

Find directions, warnings and allergens
#

Directions tell you how much to take, how often and how. Warnings and precautions tell you who should take extra care. Allergen information tells you whether the product contains, for example, fish. Read all three before you buy, not after the pack arrives.

If you have a health condition, are pregnant or breastfeeding, or take regular medication, ask a qualified health professional before adding a supplement.

Keep the lot number
#

Your pack's lot number links it to the manufacturing batch it came from. It's different from a barcode, a product code or your order number. Keep it handy: it's what you'll need to look up a lot record, and what support will ask for if something seems wrong.

Worked example

Fictional example for reading practice only. These numbers don't describe any Body Café Co. product.

An illustrative label, read in order

Here the 20 mg refers to two capsules together, so one capsule holds half that amount. The compound is named, so you can check whether 20 mg is the mineral itself or the whole compound. The pack holds 60 capsules in total.

In a minute
#

Iron bisglycinate is iron bound to two molecules of the amino acid glycine. On any iron label, the number to find is the elemental iron per serving, not the weight of the whole compound. Our label states 29 mg elemental iron per capsule, as Ferrochel® ferrous bisglycinate chelate.

BEFORE YOU TAKE IT

If you have a health condition, are pregnant or breastfeeding, or take regular medication, speak with a qualified health professional before adding a supplement. Nothing on this site is a diagnosis or personal advice.

The NIH Office of Dietary Supplements notes that accidental overdose of iron-containing products is a leading cause of fatal poisoning in children under 6. Keep any iron product out of children's reach.

SOURCE: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements — Iron: Fact Sheet for Health Professionals (updated 4 Sep 2025)

Directions, cautions and storage for our product are on its product page.

What it is
#

About the ingredient · general information

Iron is a mineral. The NIH Office of Dietary Supplements describes it as an essential component of hemoglobin, the red blood cell protein that carries oxygen. In supplements it's always bound to something else, as a salt or a chelate, and iron bisglycinate is one such form.

SOURCE: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements — Iron: Fact Sheet for Health Professionals (updated 4 Sep 2025)

Names, forms and terms
#

About the ingredient · general information

“Bis-” means two and “glycinate” refers to glycine, an amino acid. So the name describes iron bound to two glycine molecules. The NIH fact sheet groups forms like this as iron amino-acid chelates.

Because the iron is bound to glycine, the weight of iron bisglycinate isn't the weight of iron. The elemental iron is only part of it. The same source gives other iron compounds as examples: ferrous fumarate is 33% elemental iron by weight, ferrous sulfate 20% and ferrous gluconate 12%.

SOURCE: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements — Iron: Fact Sheet for Health Professionals (updated 4 Sep 2025)

About the ingredient · general information

A reviewed research summary is being prepared. Research summaries on this site are published only after specialist review, so this guide doesn't yet summarise findings or outcomes.

Research on an ingredient describes that ingredient, in the form, amount and people studied. It isn't evidence about our finished product.

What it is
#

About the ingredient · general information

Fish oil is an oil that contains omega-3 fatty acids. The NIH Office of Dietary Supplements names the main omega-3s as alpha-linolenic acid (ALA), eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA); EPA and DHA are the long-chain omega-3s found in fish oil.

Names, forms and terms
#

About the ingredient · general information

EPA and DHA are named for their structure: EPA has 20 carbon atoms and DHA 22. The same source describes a typical fish oil supplement as about 1,000 mg of fish oil containing 180 mg EPA and 120 mg DHA, and notes that amounts vary widely. So “1,000 mg fish oil” on its own doesn't tell you how much omega-3 you get.

Omega-3s in supplements come in several chemical forms: natural triglycerides, free fatty acids, ethyl esters, re-esterified triglycerides and phospholipids.

What it is
#

About the ingredient · general information

Inositol is a carbocyclic sugar alcohol. Myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol are two of its forms, and the body stores both in organs such as the kidneys, brain and liver.

SOURCE: Kiani AK, et al. From myo-inositol to D-chiro-inositol molecular pathways. Eur Rev Med Pharmacol Sci. 2021;25(5):2390–2402

Names, forms and terms
#

About the ingredient · general information

Inositol's hydroxyl groups can be arranged in nine ways, giving nine possible stereoisomers. “Myo-” and “D-chiro-” name two of them. Because they're distinct ingredients, a fair comparison needs both amounts, not just the combined total.

A ratio (for example, “40:1”) describes how the two amounts relate. It should be checked against the stated amounts of each.

In a minute
#

Two labels can name the same ingredient and still not be comparable. The form an ingredient comes in, and whether an amount refers to the whole compound or just its active part, can change what a number means.

The form is part of the ingredient's identity.
Check whether an amount is the compound or the active part.
Compare amounts in the same unit.
For oils, look at the active fatty acids, not just the total.

COMPOUND WEIGHT VERSUS ELEMENTAL IRON · PER 100 MG OF EACH COMPOUND

Ferrous fumarate
33 mg iron
Ferrous sulfate
20 mg iron
Ferrous gluconate
12 mg iron
Percentages from the NIH Office of Dietary Supplements iron fact sheet, cited in the iron guide. The same 100 mg of compound gives different amounts of iron, so compare the elemental amount.
Compound weight versus active amount
#

Minerals and some other ingredients come bound to something else. The weight of the whole compound isn't the same as the weight of the active part. The NIH Office of Dietary Supplements gives iron as an example: ferrous fumarate is 33% elemental iron by weight, ferrous sulfate 20% and ferrous gluconate 12%. So “100 mg” of one iron compound and “100 mg” of another don't contain the same amount of iron.

Creatine is similar. The same source notes that creatine monohydrate, the most widely studied form, is 88% creatine by weight.

Same nutrient, different units
#

Vitamin D can be stated in micrograms (mcg) or International Units (IU). According to the NIH Office of Dietary Supplements, 1 mcg of vitamin D equals 40 IU. Convert before you compare, so you're comparing like with like.

Named forms
#

Some vitamins come in several named forms. Vitamin D appears in supplements as D2 or D3. Vitamin K appears as K1 (phylloquinone) or as K2 menaquinones such as MK-4 or MK-7. A label should say which.

Oils: the total and the actives
#

For fish oil, the amount of oil and the amount of omega-3s are different numbers. The NIH Office of Dietary Supplements describes a typical fish oil supplement as about 1,000 mg of fish oil containing around 180 mg EPA and 120 mg DHA, and notes that amounts vary widely. Look for EPA and DHA stated separately.

Omega-3s also come in different chemical forms, including natural triglycerides, ethyl esters, re-esterified triglycerides, free fatty acids and phospholipids. Our Vitamin D3 + K2 includes omega-3 as triglycerides; its label states 200 mg total Omega-3 per softgel, including EPA 100 mg and DHA 75 mg.

Compare like with like
#

For a formula with several ingredients, compare each declared component on its own. Line up the form, the amount, the unit and the serving size. If any of these is missing, you can't make a fair comparison yet. Our product pages will use the approved quantities and wording from each label.

Worked example
#

Fictional example for reading practice only. Not Body Café Co. products or amounts.

An illustrative comparison
Label A
Example mineral, 100 mg (as compound)
Label B
Example mineral, 30 mg (elemental)
Serving A
1 capsule
Serving B
2 tablets

These numbers can't be compared directly. Label A gives the compound weight, Label B the elemental amount, and the servings differ. You'd need the compound's elemental percentage and the same serving basis first.

#
Full ingredient name and form
Compound or active amount
Unit, converted if needed
Serving size on the same basis
Each component of a formula compared separately

Serving sizes, amounts and units

How the serving, the amount and the unit fit together, so you can compare labels fairly.

2 min read

IN THIS GUIDE

1
In a minute
2

3

4
Servings per pack
5

6
Chews, softgels and capsules
7
Worked example
8
Checklist
9

In a minute
#

Three numbers do most of the work on a label: the serving size, the amount per serving and the unit. Read them together and comparisons become simple. Read one without the others and they mislead.

An amount always belongs to a serving.
A serving can be more than one unit.
Convert to the same unit before comparing.
Servings per pack = units in the pack ÷ units per serving.

SERVING ARITHMETIC · ARITHMETIC ONLY, NOT A DOSE RECOMMENDATION

Choose a product
Iron Bisglycinate
L-Theanine
Vitamin D3 + K2
Omega-3 Fish Oil
Myo & D-Chiro Inositol
Creatine Chews
Psyllium Husk

60 capsules ÷ 1 per serving = 60 servings
The label states 60 servings per pack.

Units per pack ÷ units per serving = servings per pack. Values come from each product’s label.
The serving comes first
#

Every amount on a label is an amount per serving. If the serving size is two capsules, the amount comes from both capsules together, and one capsule holds half of it.

The serving is set by the label's directions. It isn't something to guess from the front of the pack.

Same unit, then compare
#

Amounts are usually in grams (g), milligrams (mg) or micrograms (mcg). 1 g is 1,000 mg, and 1 mg is 1,000 mcg, so 0.5 mg and 500 mcg are the same amount.

Some vitamins also use International Units (IU). For vitamin D, the NIH Office of Dietary Supplements gives 1 mcg as equal to 40 IU. Convert before comparing two labels.

SOURCE: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements — Vitamin D: Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

Servings per pack
#

The pack count tells you how many units are inside. Divide it by the number of units in a serving to get the servings per pack. A pack of 60 capsules with a two-capsule serving holds 30 servings.

That's arithmetic, not a recommendation. How much to take and how often comes from the approved directions.

Percentages of a daily allowance
#

Under FSSAI's health supplement regulations, where it applies, a label shows amounts as a percentage of the ICMR recommended daily allowance, with the warning “Not to exceed the recommended daily usage”. A percentage is only meaningful next to the amount and serving it refers to.

SOURCE: FSSAI — Health Supplements, Nutraceuticals … Regulations, 2016 (FAO FAOLEX copy, version dated 29.09.2021)

Chews, softgels and capsules
#

Format changes what a unit is. A chew, a softgel and a capsule can each be a single unit, and a serving can be one or several of them. For chews, also read the nutrition information: a chew can carry sugars or sweeteners alongside its main ingredient.

Worked example
#

Chews per pack
60
Per chew
1.5 g
Servings per pack
30

The 3 g refers to two chews, so each chew holds 1.5 g. Sixty chews at two per serving make 30 servings.

Amount per serving, with unit
Same unit before comparing (mcg, mg, g, IU)
Units per pack and servings per pack
Any % of a daily allowance, read next to the amount

ESSENTIALS

Understanding evidence

Ingredient research, product testing, certification and lot reports answer different questions.

2 min read
Body Café Co. editorial
Not yet specialist-reviewed
Version 0.1 · 22 October 2026

Save guide
Print learning sheet
Copy link

IN THIS GUIDE

1
In a minute
2
Four kinds of evidence
3
How studies differ
4
Ingredient research isn't product proof
5
Testing and certification
6
What labels can't claim
7
Worked example
8
Checklist
9
Sources and versions
In a minute
#

“Backed by research”, “tested”, “certified”: each phrase points to a different kind of evidence, and each can only answer certain questions. Knowing which is which helps you read any brand's claims, including ours.

Research on an ingredient isn't research on a finished product.
Testing a product describes what's in it, not what it does.
A certification covers a stated scope and period.
A lot report describes one batch.

FOUR KINDS OF EVIDENCE, FOUR DIFFERENT QUESTIONS

01
Ingredient research

Can show: What studies found about an ingredient, in the form, amount, people and time studied.

Can’t show: That a different product, amount or person will get the same result.

02
Finished-product testing

Can show: What a sample of the product contains: identity, amount of an ingredient, named contaminants against limits.

Can’t show: What the product does in the body, or whether every pack is the same.

03
Certification

Can show: That a product or site met a defined standard, as checked by a named third party, for a stated scope and period.

Can’t show: Anything outside its scope or dates, or how well a product works.

04
Lot reports

Can show: What was tested on a sample from one manufacturing batch, by which method, against which limits.

Can’t show: Results for other batches, health outcomes, or that a single pack is authentic.

Four kinds of evidence
#

Ingredient research, finished-product testing, certification and lot reports are often blurred together. The table on the Learn hub sets out what each can establish and where it stops. In short: research studies an ingredient, testing checks a product, certification checks against a standard, and a lot report records one batch.

How studies differ
#

An observational study watches what people already do and can show that two things go together, not that one causes the other. A randomised controlled trial assigns people by chance to compare an intervention with a control, which is how cause and effect is tested. A systematic review gathers and appraises all the trials on a question, and often grades how certain the overall evidence is.

Results also depend on who was studied, the form and amount used, and for how long. A finding in one group, form or amount doesn't automatically carry over to another.

Ingredient research isn't product proof
#

Research on an ingredient tells you about that ingredient, in the form, amount and people studied. It doesn't show that a particular finished product, with its own formula and amount, will have the same result. That's why our guides keep general ingredient information separate from facts about our products, and why we don't turn research into promises.

Testing and certification
#

Testing a finished product can check its identity, how much of an ingredient it contains, and whether named contaminants are below a limit. It doesn't test what the product does in your body. A certification is a third party's statement that something met a defined standard; read what it covers, who issued it and when. Body Café Co. doesn't currently claim any certification.

What labels can't claim
#

Under FSSAI's health supplement regulations, a health supplement can't claim to prevent, treat or cure a disease. Treat that kind of promise as a warning sign, whoever makes it.

SOURCE: FSSAI — Health Supplements, Nutraceuticals … Regulations, 2016 (FAO FAOLEX copy, version dated 29.09.2021)

Worked example
#

General guide for reading claims. Not a statement about any Body Café Co. product.

Matching the question to the evidence
“What does this ingredient do?”
Ingredient research, in its stated form and amount
“Is the amount on the label in the pack?”
Finished-product testing
“Was it made to a stated standard?”
Certification, within its scope and dates
“What was found in my batch?”
The lot report for your lot number

Each question has its own kind of evidence. A strong answer to one doesn't answer the others.

Checklist
#
Which kind of evidence is this?
Ingredient or finished product?
Which form, amount and people were studied?
What scope and dates does a certification cover?
Which lot does a report describe?

HELP · RETURNS · BODY CAFÉ CO.

Can I return something I no longer want?
Help Centre
Returns
Can I return something I no longer want?
We don’t accept change-of-mind returns.
Supplements are consumed, so for everyone’s safety we only take back items that arrived damaged, wrong, missing, faulty or expired.

Report a problem within 7 days of delivery from the order page, and we’ll arrange a refund or replacement.

bodyText:
HELP · ORDERS · BODY CAFÉ CO.

I ordered without an account. How do I see my order?
Help Centre
Orders
I ordered without an account. How do I see my order?
In the same browser, your order is listed under Account.
To keep it, sign in with the mobile number you used at checkout.
Signing in uses a one-time code sent to your mobile number.
Orders from that browser session that used the same number join your account.

We don’t show order details to anyone who can’t verify the mobile number on the order.

bodyText:
HELP · ORDERS · BODY CAFÉ CO.

Can I change an order after placing it?
Help Centre
Orders
Can I change an order after placing it?
Orders can’t be edited once placed.
Before dispatch you can cancel and order again; for a delivery address change, contact us with the order reference.

We’ll tell you whether a change is still possible. A change isn’t confirmed until we reply on your case.
